summary: Internal enablement with Caldera Health to walk through a customer-facing deck, rehearse messaging around failover and Dedicated fallback, and draft a short runbook for production incident scenarios. Focus: crisp security messaging, predictable performance, and demo scripts that show graceful degradation to cheaper/backup variants.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-26
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~90 minutes (recording truncated around Q&A)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Rizzo (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Caldera Head of AI), Tom Becker (Caldera Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Caldera Security)
Shared: internal deck: https://redwood.internal/sales/deck/redacted-failover-v2 (redacted link)

Auto-summary (presented at top):
- Trim the first two slides to remove heavy infra jargon; lead with cost/latency tradeoff and a one-line guarantee about failover latency.
- Add an example incident timeline and a 3-step runbook for app owners.
- Replace technical term "K-V cache" with "KV cache (key-value cache)" and add a footnote about prefix caching.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya (AE): Okay everyone, welcome — thanks for carving out the time. We'll do a quick pass through the customer-facing deck, then run a 10 minute failover demo script, and finish with Q&A. 
[00:18] Jon (SE): Hi all, Jon here. I'll be walking the failover flow and then we'll roleplay the demo handoff. Quick note: I'm starting the sample notebook for the fallback path. There might be a few pauses while I pull the link.
[00:35] Lina (Customer): Thanks, Maya. We're really focused on making sure our patient-facing summaries never show hallucinations and we want a robust fallback path if latency spikes. So... latency thresholds, SLOs, and audit trail are very important.
[00:50] Priya (Customer Security): And from security, we care about audit logs, KMS integration, and who can see tokens. Also need SOC 2 language in the deck.
[01:05] Maya: Great, let's jump in. Slide 1 is our one-liner, slide 2 is the problem statement — Jon, quick reaction?
[01:22] Jon: The problem slide reads fine but it's dense. Suggest we rephrase "inference economics" to "predictable cost per user" — customers nod to cost. Also the line about "KV cash" — I mean, K-V cash — gets misread, so let's change to "KV cache (key-value cache)" and add one visual.
[01:45] Tom: Agree. Also on slide 4 where you show a 200ms latency target, our reality is 250–400ms p95 under load; we need to be honest or else the demo looks suspect.
[02:10] Maya: Good call. Proposal: call out typical p95 ranges for small vs large prompts and use a small table.
[02:28] Jon: And show the fallback policy: "If p95 > 350ms for 2 consecutive minutes, route to Dedicated variant or lower-seq model with stable latency".
[02:45] Lina: I like that. But can you quantify the quality drop when we go to the lower-seq model? Our UX team needs numbers.
[03:05] Jon: We'll include a quality delta slide — BLEU-style isn't right for chat, but we can show typical token-level ROUGE-ish diff and some human eval examples.
[03:25] Maya: Ok next — demo script. We'll roleplay. Jon you'll be the SE and Lina you'll be the customer, is that right?
[03:40] Jon: Right. Script start: "OK Lina, I'm going to simulate an incident where the hosted endpoint is saturated, and you'll see the UI switch to 'Awaiting fallback' then to 'Dedicated (fallback)'." 
[03:55] Lina: Sounds good.
[04:08] [04:00] Jon: Start demo. I'm hitting the host load generator. The console shows 503s then a 30 second grace period. We trigger the policy: fallback to Dedicated.
[04:25] Priya: Quick interruption — during that handoff, what happens to logs? Do we lose trace IDs? We need continuity for audits.
[04:40] Jon: Excellent question. We forward trace IDs into the fallback path; the platform preserves request IDs and appends a "fallback=true" tag to the audit event. We'll put that in the runbook.
[05:00] Tom: If there's a region failure, can we route to a different region with lower compliance controls? Our compliance team would not like cross-border by default.
[05:18] Maya: We'll add explicit gating: per-customer policy for cross-region fallback, with an opt-in flag. For Caldera, default stays in-region.
[05:35] Lina: Okay. One thing: when we demo fallbacks, we should illustrate user-visible differences, not just logs.
[05:50] Jon: Agreed. We'll show a short latency chart and show a small sample answer exhibiting the change — e.g. shorter completion or paraphrased reply.
[06:08] [06:00] Maya: Now slide surgery — slide 7 is product architecture. Jon, I think this is too dense for an exec. Simplify to three boxes: "Request routing", "Serving runtime", "Customer isolation (VPC/Dedicated)".
[06:28] Jon: And annotate the serving runtime with bullets: batched kernels, KV cache, quantized variants. But caution: "quantized" can scare some buyers, so use language "size-optimized model variants".
[06:48] Priya: Also add a note: KMS/HSM integration and zero-knowledge claims — don't overpromise encryption.
[07:05] Maya: We'll add a slide with bullet points under compliance.
[07:20] Lina: How do we address competitor shoves, like "they have in-region only managed solutions"? We sometimes get asked why not Anthropic or OpenAI.
[07:34] Jon: Positioning: say Redwood gives deployment flexibility (hosted, Dedicated, Private) and predictable throughput with runbook-backed SLAs. Avoid direct comparisons of model quality — focus on operational guarantees.
[07:50] Maya: Ok, let's script that as a two-line comparison: "Model access vs Serving guarantees".
[08:05] [08:00] Roleplay segment two: Failure escalation. Jon, read the runbook steps out loud.
[08:12] Jon: Step 1 — Detect: monitor p95 and error rate; if p95 > threshold for N minutes, open incident. Step 2 — Notify: notify SRE + AE, tag incident with trace IDs. Step 3 — Circuit: auto-route to fallback variant and toggle burst capacity if available. Step 4 — Postmortem and quality check where we sample generated outputs for hallucination risk.
[08:45] Tom: For step 3, can we toggle autoscale while keeping affinity to customer tokens? We need data isolation.
[09:00] Jon: Yes, Dedicated pools preserve data isolation; autoscale only within the customer's reserved capacity. We'll make that explicit.
[09:18] Priya: And we need to include the retention windows and how to purge keys from KMS.
[09:30] Maya: Action: Jon, add a KMS/retention appendix to the runbook.
[09:42] Jon: Noted.
[10:00] [10:00] Maya: Moving on to objection handling. Common objection: "Your fallback reduces quality". How do we answer?
[10:12] Jon: Say: "We design fallback variants to minimize semantic degradation; we publish quantified quality deltas on common workloads and provide a canary roll for you to validate on your prompts." 
[10:28] Lina: We want to run that canary ourselves. How long does a canary take?
[10:40] Jon: Typically 48–72 hours with representative traffic; for a small sample we can do it in 24 hours.
[10:52] Maya: We'll include a canary playbook slide with steps and expected metrics.
[11:08] [11:00] Priya: Another security Q — what about token leakage if we route between hosted and Dedicated? Are tokens rotated?
[11:22] Jon: The platform rotates ephemeral tokens on route and we mask tokens in logs. We'll add explicit statements about token rotation and log redaction.
[11:40] Tom: On the slide about costs, can we show a quick ROI calc? Our CFO wants to see monthly cost delta between hosted and Dedicated.
[11:55] Maya: We'll prepare a simple table with sample qps and cost per 1M tokens for each mode. Jon, can you help with numbers?
[12:08] Jon: Yes. Also include a note about model quantization and batching effects on effective cost.
[12:20] [12:00] Roleplay — rapid-fire rebuttals. Maya throws a typical hostile question: "Why shouldn't we just run open source yourself?"
[12:30] Jon: "You could, but you'd trade off predictable SLOs, continuous optimization for kernels and MLOps, and need to build storage, KV cache management and security controls — which takes months."
[12:50] Lina: The "months" claim is strong — perhaps swap to "tens of weeks" with a caution.
[13:02] Maya: Good nuance.
[13:18] [13:00] Break in recording — short silence while we reorganize slides.
[13:45] Jon: Back on. Slide 12: Demo checklist — ensure API keys have the right scope, enable audit logs, start load generator at step 1.
[14:05] Priya: Add a pre-demo security checklist item: verify SSO users cannot escalate to developer scope.
[14:20] Maya: We'll add that to the pre-demo slide.
[14:35] [14:00] Live rehearsal: Maya plays AE, Jon does the technical walkthrough.
[14:50] Maya (AE, roleplay): "Tom we've seen p95 spike — I'm going to flip the fallback; you should see the user answer shorten but stay relevant."
[15:05] Tom (Customer, roleplay): "I see it — response is a bit shorter but acceptable."
[15:20] Jon: Note: capture both versions and put them in the appendix for the customer to audit.
[15:35] Lina: That appendix will be key.
[15:50] [15:00] Audience question: "How do you handle model rollbacks?"
[15:12] Jon: We do canary traffic, metrics guardrails, and a hot rollback path that pins the model version while we investigate. We'll add a rollback flowchart slide.
[16:00] Maya: Time check — we've got ~20 minutes for Q&A and runbook drafting. Let's start drafting a one-page runbook now. Jon will type; I'll narrate.
[16:20] Jon: I'll share the runbook doc link in chat. (link pasted)
[16:30] [16:00] Runbook draft (live read):
- Title: Caldera Health — Redwood failover runbook (redacted)
- Purpose: Ensure minimal user impact when hosted endpoints underperform or regional capacity is constrained.
- Owner: Caldera SRE + Redwood SE
- Detection: Alert when p95 > 350ms for 2 mins or error rate > 5%
- Immediate action: Trigger automatic routing to Dedicated fallback, scale burst capacity if reserved, notify on-call, start sampling 50 outputs for QA
- Recovery: Monitor quality metrics for 30 minutes; if quality degradation > threshold, initiate rollback to previous model version and open postmortem
- Post-incident: 72-hour follow-up for human evaluation and adjust canary thresholds

[17:10] Priya: Embedded in here we need a step for key revocation in case of compromise.
[17:25] Jon: Add step: Revoke ephemeral tokens and rotate KMS key material as per policy.
[17:38] Maya: Let's mark that as high priority. Action item: put key rotation verbiage in runbook.
[17:50] [17:00] Conversation drifts to messaging: what's the headline on slide 1?
[18:05] Maya: Proposed headline: "Predictable inference, protected data — deploy where you need, fail safely when you don't." Thoughts?
[18:20] Lina: Strong. Maybe cut "when you don't"— sounds negative. How about "fail safely when needed".
[18:34] Jon: Or "protecting latency and privacy at scale".
[18:48] Maya: We'll A/B test two headlines in the deck.
[19:05] [19:00] Quick script tweak: revise the objection-handling cheat sheet with three archetypes: Security-conscious, Cost-focused, Platform-engineer.
[19:18] Tom: Make sure the Platform-engineer cheat has concrete API examples.
[19:30] Jon: I'll add a one-liner with curl and SDK example.
[19:45] [20:00] Final roleplay: Maya closes with next steps to the customer.
[20:12] Maya: Lina, Tom, Priya — we'll send the redacted runbook and new deck by Friday, Jon will prepare the Dedicated fallback demo script, and Tom will send us latency logs to set thresholds. Any other asks?
[20:30] Lina: Please also send the canary playbook and the appendix with before/after sample outputs.
[20:45] Priya: And a short paragraph about token rotation and data retention for our legal team.
[21:00] Maya: Will do.
[21:12] Jon: One last micro-note: in the appendix, do not include live customer PII; use synthetic examples.
[21:28] Tom: Acknowledged.
[21:40] [21:00] Quick improv: Jon suggests a short chart to show expected token cost delta for the fallback event. Maya: add to appendix.
[22:00] Conversation slows; people thank each other and start to leave.
[22:30] End recording (approx).

Recap / Explicit next steps (repeated at the end):
- Maya: Send redacted runbook and updated deck (by 2025-03-28).
- Jon: Draft Dedicated fallback demo script and appendix examples (by 2025-04-02).
- Tom: Share latency profile and sample prompts (by 2025-04-01).
- Action: Add KMS/rotation and pre-demo security checklist into the deck.

Notes on transcription quality: background noise around [13:00] caused a short drop, some words transcribed as "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache", and Product names sometimes split (e.g., "Red wood Private").
questions: What is the expected p95 threshold we should commit to for canary?
Can we demonstrate rollback in the next demo?
Will Redwood rotate tokens during fallback and how is that documented?
